disclaimer: All records document ANCIENT aqueous alteration or fluvial/lacustrine processes. None constitutes evidence of present-day liquid water or extractable water ice. Evidence classes: direct_observation (in-situ rover instrument), remote_sensing_indication (orbital spectroscopy), inference (geomorphology / literature interpretation).

water_ice.statement: No near-surface water-ice detection exists for Jezero crater (18.4 N). Orbital neutron spectrometers (Mars Odyssey GRS/NS) show low equatorial hydrogen (< ~5 wt% WEH) consistent with hydrated minerals rather than ice, and no SHARAD subsurface reflector attributed to ice has been reported here. Ice stability models place the equatorward limit of shallow ground ice near 40-50 degrees latitude.
sources: Feldman, W.C. et al. (2004) JGR 109, E09006
Piqueux, S. et al. (2019) GRL 46 (ice stability)

evidence.name: Fe/Mg smectite clays in the western delta
evidence.interpretation: Clays within delta bottomset/foreset strata indicate detrital or in-situ alteration in a long-lived aqueous environment.
evidence.uncertainty: Spectral detection of hydrated phyllosilicate is robust; exact stratigraphic position inferred from HiRISE.
sources: Ehlmann, B.L. et al. (2008) Nature Geosci. 1, 355

evidence.name: Mg-carbonate 'Marginal unit'
evidence.interpretation: Strongest carbonate absorptions in Jezero follow the inner western margin; possible lake-shoreline or altered volcanic unit.
evidence.uncertainty: Carbonate abundance not quantified from orbit; formation setting debated.

evidence.name: Olivine-carbonate crater floor
evidence.interpretation: Regional olivine-rich unit partially altered to carbonate (NE Syrtis / Jezero floor).
evidence.uncertainty: Patchy exposure under dust and eolian cover.
sources: Brown, A.J. et al. (2020) JGR Planets 125

evidence.name: Séítah carbonate, sulfate and perchlorate in igneous cumulate
evidence.interpretation: Water percolated through olivine cumulate rocks depositing salts; at least two episodes of aqueous alteration.
evidence.uncertainty: Timing of alteration relative to lake uncertain.

evidence.name: Wildcat Ridge sulfates + aromatic organics
evidence.interpretation: Fine-grained delta-front mudstone with sulfate cement and aromatic organic molecules.
evidence.uncertainty: Organics are not evidence of life; abiotic origins possible.

evidence.name: Cheyava Falls 'leopard spots' (Bright Angel)
evidence.interpretation: Redox reaction fronts in mudstone that on Earth are often microbially mediated; potential biosignature pending sample return.
evidence.uncertainty: Abiotic pathways cannot be excluded in situ.

evidence.name: Western delta and lake-level indicators
evidence.interpretation: Gilbert-type delta with topsets at ~ -2490 m implies a lake at least 100 m deep that persisted long enough to build the fan; later floods carried boulders.
evidence.uncertainty: Lake duration estimates range from decades-scale episodes to >10^4 years.

evidence.name: Neretva and Sava Vallis inlet valleys
evidence.interpretation: Valley networks delivering water and sediment from a ~ 30,000 km^2 watershed.
evidence.uncertainty: Discharge estimates vary by an order of magnitude.

evidence.name: THEMIS night-IR thermal inertia contrast (floor vs delta)
evidence.interpretation: Bright (warm) night-time floor = bedrock/high thermal inertia; dark delta surfaces = finer sediments. Useful for trafficability, not a water indicator.
evidence.uncertainty: Qualitative in this build; no quantitative TI values ingested.
